decisions.reason: As a resin injection unit it is close to our existing machinery knowledge base, and its own product page in both 2018 and 2019 suggests enough early market traction to justify further learning and incremental improvement.

This product also fits strongly with our established application and engineering capabilities, so under an absorptive-capacity logic we would usually retain it unless later evidence clearly showed weak demand.
An automatic airless spray gun is highly related to our core coating-equipment competences, making it easier for us to interpret feedback, refine the design, and continue commercializing it.
The manual airless spray gun is a close extension of the firm's existing mechanical and application know-how, and its continued standalone presentation through 2019 supports keeping it on the market.

The air-assisted airless spray gun remains within our core technological domain, so we are well placed to absorb user feedback and improve it, although variant overlap creates some rationalization risk.

The data logger is less central to our traditional machinery knowledge base and already lost prominence from a standalone page to a mere mention in 2019, indicating weaker fit and lower confidence in our ability to scale and improve it commercially.
